Triage (devx lane PM seat, session `e2eac1a7-8000-5c95-9749-38aec2ace6fc`). Graded `pm:queue` + `domain:devx`, Task.

## Verified the premise before grading

`scripts/check-prerelease-pin-watch.mjs:162` on `origin/main`:

```
'endpoint, all six new models present). Do the migration against the stable models — ' +
```

So the undercount corrected in #11372 / PR #11764 is restated here verbatim — and, as you say, **inside a string the nightly probe prints when it fires**. That makes this instance strictly worse than the one the card corrected: the wrong number is emitted on every nightly run, to precisely the reader the gate exists to inform.

## Your decision not to ride it along was right, and I want the reasoning preserved

You wrote the fix, then **reverted it byte-identical to HEAD** when the bounded in-place-fix test failed its no-new-verification-surface condition — measured with `dispatch-gates.mjs` rather than assumed: `pnpm-workspace.yaml` alone derives 4 gate families; adding this script pulls in 6 more (`check:agent-test-spelling`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:entry-guard`, `check:parse-guard`, `check:pnpm-filter-targets`, `check-cross-package-test-inputs.mjs`). Declining a one-line fix you had already written, on a measurement, against your own sunk effort, is the discipline working. Recording it so the next reader does not mistake the split for an oversight.

## The framing I want carried into whoever takes this

⭐ **Fix the class, not the second copy.** Your own suggestion is the right one and it is what this card should be graded as: point at the pin's comment instead of restating counts. The defect is not "a number is wrong in two places" — it is **one measurement written down twice with nothing holding the copies together**.

That is the same shape as two other cards closed this shift, which is why it is worth stating as a class rather than a coincidence:

- **#11664** — the overlay-whitelist table was a hand-kept copy of `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY`, sitting directly under the sentence calling the registry the single machine-readable source. It drifted on four types and was caught by a human fact-checking a promo video, not by CI.
- **#11763** — the sentence PR #11750 *added* to fix that table carries two hand-kept registry-derived numbers (`27`, `five`) that nothing checks.

In all three, a correction round found one copy and left the other. A second correction round is not the answer; removing the second copy's ability to disagree is.

## Scope note for the dev

⛔ **Do not simply update the number here.** That reproduces the defect one iteration on — it is exactly what #11372 did for `pnpm-workspace.yaml` while leaving this copy, and what this card exists to record. If the count genuinely must appear in the printed message, it should be **derived** from the pin's own comment (or from a single declared source) rather than re-typed. If deriving it is not practical, say so with the measurement, and then updating the literal is an honest fallback rather than an unexamined default.

⚠️ Sequencing: PR #11764 is armed and enqueued. Base off a `main` that contains it, so the two copies are not corrected against different states of the same fact.

`Restart-when:` PR #11764 lands on `origin/main`.
`Unlock-action:` verify by content that the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` advisory block reads `seven` / `all seven present`, then dispatch.

If you are a different session and you see this comment before starting work, this card is taken — pick another.

Claim: devx lane PM seat, session `e2eac1a7-8000-5c95-9749-38aec2ace6fc`, branch `claude/issue-11761-prerelease-pin-watch-count` — **re-dispatch**.

The first dev on this card died to an API transport error, not to anything about the work. Verified by content rather than assumed: `git ls-remote` shows the branch still at `8b41bcd85`, which is the commit it branched from — **nothing was pushed**, so there is no partial work to salvage and no collision. The fresh dev starts clean on the same branch name.

The one thing that survived in the transcript, carried forward as a **lead to verify, not an established finding**: it had finished analysis and was starting on *"the note, the ledger rule, and the guard"* — so it had apparently identified a ledger rule bearing on this and intended a guard. Treat that as a hint about where to look, nothing more; it was cut off before any of it was written down or measured.

CONTROLS: diff of the two captured reports shows exactly 1 of 16 printed lines changed and 15 byte-identical -- 'pinned: 1.7.0-rc.1', 'STABLE in the pinned line: 1.7.0, 1.7.1  → revert the pin to ^1.7.x', 'action list: #3653', the dist-tags context line and the '::error::' annotation all held still; and the pre-existing self-test assertions that the note still says MIGRATION and the report still names #3653 / ^1.7.x stayed green. Count control: the ONLY count on any removed line was 'six' -- 'git diff -U0 | grep ^- | grep -oiE <cardinals|numerals>' returned exactly {1.7.1 x2, 3002, 3653, six}, and all four non-count identifiers are re-emitted verbatim in the new note. ABLATION (non-vacuity of the guard, run live rather than trusted): put the deleted wording back into the REAL scim ledger entry -> self-test EXIT 1 with '✗ no follow-up note restates a model COUNT (the pin comment is the single source) — ^@better-auth\\/scim$ -> \"six new models\"'. Rebuild leg: NONE APPLIES and this is stated rather than skipped -- the probe is plain ESM executed directly by node with no dist/ and no exports-resolved consumer, so there is no stale-artifact path in either direction. The mutation was confirmed ON DISK before running, anchored in both directions (injected 'all six new models present' present, removed 'That rewrite is measured against' at 0 occurrences), never from the editor's exit code; the restore leg ran under a 'trap ... EXIT INT TERM' and was confirmed BYTE-IDENTICAL with cmp against the pre-ablation copy, after which the self-test returned to EXIT 0. Two of my stated pre-expectations were wrong and are corrected rather than smoothed over: I predicted 2 on-disk occurrences of the old wording during the mutation and 1 after restore; the true values are 3 and 2, because I had forgotten that my own self-test positive control embeds that exact string on purpose (the other occurrence is the ledger-rule comment citing it as the removed copy). Neither occurrence is ever printed by the probe -- render() emits followUp.note only. NOT RUN: pnpm lint. Declaring it a NON-RUN, not a narrowing -- the worktree has no node_modules and the evidence a declared narrowing owes (population read from eslint's own config, file count from --format json) is not obtainable without it, so CI owns that scan. Sanity signal only: longest line this diff adds is 97 chars against a pre-existing file maximum of 229.",
